issues: No sign of getting around the measurement. The PLS projection is fit on the training fold only (train X and rank-transformed train y). The test molecules are only passed through transform, and no test labels are used. There is no file or network access and no pasted values.

No bug that would make the result meaningless. The PLS scores are standardized with training-fold statistics only. The three kernels are averaged, so K_train stays positive semi-definite. K_test has the shape (n_test, n_train) that SVR(kernel='precomputed') expects.

Likely reason for the regression: the PLS kernel is built from labels. On the training fold it lines up with y by construction, so it overfits there and does not carry over to unseen scaffolds. It also reduces the weight of the Tanimoto and descriptor kernels from 1/2 each to 1/3 each.

The z value checks out. Difference = 0.5281 - 0.4690 = 0.0591. SE = 0.0070*sqrt(1 + 1/2) ≈ 0.00857, so |z| ≈ 6.89. The harness reports -6.867, which matches up to rounding. Here the negative sign means the candidate is worse. Rejecting it is correct: the loss rose by about 0.059, far beyond the noise.
